GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.  79 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 01.12.2025 
 
India's Ranking in Forest Area 
 
79.   SHRI DHAIRYASHEEL SAMBHAJIRAO MANE: 
        SHRI CHAVAN RAVINDRA VASANTRAO:            
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether it is true that India has been ranked ninth country in the world in terms of total 
forest area by the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) in its Global 
Forest Resources Assessment 2025; 
(b) if so, the details of India’s total forest cover as per the said assessment and its 
comparison with the previous report; 
(c) the extent to which ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ initiative by the Prime Minister has been 
          successful in increasing the forest area in the country since the beginning of the said 
initiative; and     
(d) the details of other major initiatives and schemes/programmes implemented/being 
implemented by the Government to increase green cover in the country during the last 
three years and the current year?                      
 
                                                                   ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (b)  As per the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organisation’s Global Forest 
Resources Assessment (GFRA)  2025, released on 22 October 2025, India has been ranked 
ninth in the world in terms of total forest area. This marks an improvement from the previous 
assessment, in which India was ranked tenth.  
 
Further, Forest Survey of India (FSI), Dehradun, an organ ization under the Ministry of 
Environment, Forest and Climate Change, carries out the assessment of forest and tree cover 
of the country biennially and the findings are published in the India State of Forest Report 
(ISFR). The forest cover assessment is a wall-to-wall mapping exercise based on remote 
sensing supported by intensive ground verification and field data from the National Forest 
Inventory. As per ISFR 2023, the total forest and tree cover of the country is 8,27,356.95 square 
kilometer which is 25.17% of the geographical area of the country.  
 
(c) to (d)   A plantation campaign “ एक पेड़ म ाँ के न म #Plant4Mother” has been launched on 
the occasion of World Environment Day 2024 and in the current year also to undertake 
plantation activities across the  country.  This campaign follows the “Whole of Government” 
and “Whole of Society” approach with participation of all stakeholders for increasing the green 
cover in the country. The campaign has contributed large scale plantation aiding the 
enhancement of green cover in the country. 

In addition, the Ministry provides technical and financial support to the States /UTs for 
protection, conservation and management of forests in the country. This includes funds from 
the Central Government under various schemes and programmes such as National Mission for 
a Green India (GIM), Forest Fire Prevention and Management Scheme (FPM), Nagar Van 
Yojana (NVY), Integrated Development of Wildlife Habitats and Mangrove Initiative for 
Shoreline Habitats and Tangible Incomes (MISHTI). Afforestation is also carried out by the 
States/UTs under the Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority 
(CAMPA).  The funds provided under the various schemes support the efforts of States and 
Union Territories to enhance forest and tree cover through ecological restoration measures such 
as afforestation within and outside forest areas, forest landscape restoration, habitat 
improvement, soil and water conservation, protection activities, and other related interventions.

SCHOOLS INFRASTRUCTURE IN RAJASTHAN  
 
†8. Shri Lumbaram Choudhary: 
   
 
     Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of the concrete steps taken by the Government to address the problem of  
infrastructure like computer labs, science labs, libraries, toilets for girl students, drinking 
water and shortage of teachers in Rajasthan especially Jalore and Sirohi districts; and 
 
(b) the strategy of the Government to make the examination system more transparent and  
reliable so that students may get quality education and secure their educational future? 
 
    
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a): Education is in the concurrent list of the Constitution and most of the schools are 
under administrative jurisdiction of concerned States & UTs . Under the Centrally Sponsored 
schemes like Samagra Shiksha , STARS and PM SHRI, States and UTs are supported for 
strengthening of existing government schools, and for creation and augmentation of 
infrastructure facilities like Additional Classrooms, Toilets for Boys/Girls/CWSN, Drinking 
Water, Electricity, Boundar y Walls, Library, ICT and Digital Classrooms, based on the gaps 
determined from Unified District Information System for Education (UDISE) database and 
proposals received from respective State/UT. The requirement of infrastructural facilities in 
schools are  worked out every year by the respective State/Union Territory on incremental 
basis depending on their need and priority and reflected in their Annual Work Plan and 
Budget (AWP&B). These plans are then appraised and approved/estimated by Project 
Approval B oard (PAB) in consultation with the States and Union Territories as per the 
programmatic and financial norms of the scheme, physical and financial progress of works 
sanctioned earlier and availability of budgetary resources.  
  

The details of infrastructure progress under Samagra Shiksha  for the State of Rajasthan 
including the districts of Jalore and Sirohi, for the years 2018-19 to 2025-26 is as under:

(b): Examinations fall under the purview of School education boards, majority of  which 
come under the jurisdiction of respective States/UTs . On its part, the Ministry of Education 
through the National Assessment Centre - PARAKH in NCERT, has undertaken an extensive 
study into ‘Equivalence of Boards’, with an aim to harmonise standard s in five key domains 
of education viz; Administration, Curriculum, Assessment, Infrastructure, and Inclusiveness, 
across all recognized school boards in India. Key findings and policy recommendations from 
the exercise, can be accessed at  
https://ncert.nic.in/parakh/pdf/Equivalence_of_Boards_Report.pdf.  
 
In order to implement the recommendations for achieving equivalence, especially in the 
domain of assessment, the Ministry of  Education, through PARAKH,NCERT has been 
providing technical, financial and capacity building support to States/UTs. Such support is 
extended in the form of training workshops for paper setters and examiners on competency -
based assessment, preparation of guidelines, blueprints and standardised templates for 
preparing question papers and question banks, and funding for implementing Holistic 
Progress Cards (HPC), digitisation of boards and development of professional cadre of paper 
setters among other interventions. 
 
Further, to expedite equivalence among school education boards, the Ministry of Education 
through Gazette Notification No. 1 -22/2024-PMP.6 issued in Sep 2025, has assigned the 
responsibility of granting equivalence for Class 10 and 12 certificates of all recognised Boards 
to PARAKH, NCERT.

of Tamil Nadu for development of new ecotourism destinations in 
Dharmapuri and adjoining areas such as Hogenakkal and the Cauvery 
Wildlife region; 
(d) the details of the funds approved, released and utilized for such projects 
during the last three years and the current year; and 
(e) the details of the steps taken/being taken to promote ecotourism in 
Dharmapuri through digital campaigns and community -based tourism 
initiatives? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF TOURISM          (SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) to (e):  Development and promotion of tourism destinations and products 
is primarily undertaken by the concerned State Government (SG)/Union 
Territory Administration (UTA). However, the Ministry of Tourism through its 
central sector schemes of ‘Swadesh Darshan (SD) , Swadesh Darshan 2.0 
(SD2.0)’, ‘Challenge Based Destination Development (CBDD), a sub -scheme of 
Swadesh Darshan scheme and ‘Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual Heritage 
Augmentation Drive (PRASHAD)’ complements the efforts of tourism 
infrastructure development in the country by extending financial assistance 
to the SGs/UTAs in synergy with the scheme guidelines, receipt of the project 
proposals from the concerned State Government/Union Territory 
Administration, availability of funds etc. Ministry of Tourism has revamped the 

Swadesh Darshan Scheme as Swadesh Darshan 2.0 (SD2.0) with the objective 
to develop sustainable tourism destinations.   
 
Government of India under its ‘Special Assistance to States for Capital 
Investment (SASCI) – Development of Iconic Tourist Centres to Global Scale’ 
sanctioned 40 projects in 23 States for Rs.3295.76 Crore in the country 
including Tamil Nadu in Financial Year 2024-25, with the primary objective to 
comprehensively develop iconic tourist centres in the country, branding and 
marketing them at global scale.  
 
In addition, the Ministry under its Assistance to Central Agencies for Tourism 
Infrastructure Development (ACATID) scheme also provides financial 
assistance to central agencies for development of tourism projects.  
 
The details of the projects sanctioned under SD, SD2.0, CBDD, PRASHAD, 
SASCI and ACATID schemes in the state of Tamil Nadu is annexed.  Presently, 
there is no proposal under consideration to sanction new projects at eco -
tourism destinations.   
 
In addition, Ministry of Tourism promotes various tourist destinations and 
products of the country including those in Tamil Nadu in domestic and 
international markets in a holistic manner under the brand line of ‘Incredible 
India’.  Such promotions are und ertaken through various ongoing initiatives 
such as social media posts, promotional website, tourism related events, 
extending support to tourism related fairs and festivals, participation in road 
shows etc.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION AND LITERACY 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 81 
ANSWERED ON 01.12.2025 
 
Increasing of Kendriya Vidyalayas 
 
81.     SHRI KOTA SRINIVASA POOJARY: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the details of steps being taken by the Government to increase the number 
of Kendriya Vidyalayas under the jurisdiction of the Union Government to 
at least three KVs per district, which is beneficial for the children of the poor 
people in the country; 
(b) whether the Government has taken note of the concerns of parents 
regarding the shortage of staff and the vacant post of a Head Master at the 
Kendriya Vidyalaya in Balehonnur located in Chikkamagaluru dist rict of 
Karnataka; and 
(c) if so, the details of steps initiated by the Government to appoint full -time 
staff in the said Kendriya Vidyalaya? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a)  At present, 1289 KVs are functioning across the Country including 03 
abroad. Opening of new Kendriya Vidyalayas (KVs) is a continuous process. KVs 
are opened primarily to cater to the educational needs of wards of transferable 
Central Government employees including Defence and Par a-military personnel 
by providing a common programme of education throughout the country and are 
not a service area school based on district’s geography . Proposals for opening 
of new KVs may be sponsored by Ministries or Departments of the Government 
of India/State Governments/ Union Territories Administrations, with commitment 

to provide requisite extent of land and suitable rent-free temporary 
accommodation for setting up a new KV as per norms. KVs are not opened area 
wise/ tehsil wise/ district wise/state wise. In the year 2024, opening of 85 new 
KVs and expansion of one existing KV and in the year 2025, opening of 57 new 
KVs have been approved by the Government of India based on the emergence 
of requirement. 
(b) & (c) Vacancies keep on arising due to ope ning of new KVs, retirement, 
resignation, promotion of employees, transfer, employees going on lien to 
another department and up -gradation of schools. Filling up of vacancies is a 
continuous process and efforts are made to fill up the vacancies as per the 
provisions of the relevant recruitment rules. Teachers are also engaged on 
contractual basis for temporary duration by Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan to 
ensure that the teaching-learning process is not hampered.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

Restoration of Mangrove Areas under MISHTI Scheme in Tamil Nadu  
 
82.  SHRI S JAGATHRATCHAKAN: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to 
state: 
(a) the current status of implementation of the Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats 
and Tangible Incomes (MISHTI) scheme in Tamil Nadu, including the total area 
identified, restored and under restoration so far, along with the timeline for completion;  
(b) whether the MISHTI scheme has incorporated traditional ecological knowledge and 
practices of coastal communities in Tamil Nadu as part of its restoration strategy and if 
so, the details thereof;  
(c) the measures taken to ensure ecological sustainability, biodiversity conservation and 
long term maintenance of restored mangrove areas in Tamil Nadu under the MISHTI 
framework; and  
(d)  the details of the capacity -building, training and l ivelihood enhancement initiatives 
undertaken for local fishermen, women’s self -help groups and farmers under the 
scheme in Tamil Nadu? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 (a) to (d)   As a part of Budget Announcement 2023 -24, the Mangrove Initiative for 
Shoreline Habitats & Tangible Incomes (MISHTI) was launched to promote and restore 
mangroves and enhance the resilience of coastal ecosystems. Implementation of the scheme 
is undertaken based on proposals submitted by the coastal States/UTs, through convergence 
with various schemes including State/National CAMPA, MGNREGS and State Plans. The 
MISHTI program encompasses both core activities, such as plantation and restoration,  and 
support activities, which include livelihood diversification, awareness generation and 
capacity building, research and development, publicity and outreach, monitoring and 
evaluation, and the promotion of ecotourism through Self -Help Groups (SHGs) and are taken 
up as per the plans received from the States under MISHTI. The State/UT -wise details 
including Tamil Nadu are provided in Annexure 1. 

The Tamil Nadu Forest Department has undertaken large -scale mangrove restoration with 
community involvement. Fro m 2022 –23 to 2024 –25, 95 hectares of new mangroves were 
planted under NABARD, Green Tamil Nadu Mission (GTM), and NHAI schemes using 
modified fish-bone designs. Additionally, 250 hectares of degraded mangrove forests were 
restored under GTM and Centrally S ponsored Schemes (CSS), and 52,000 mangrove 
seedlings were planted using linear methods. So far, an area of 22,560.34 ha has been taken 
up through convergence across 13 States/UTs for plantation and restoration of degraded 
mangroves with 1082 ha in Tamil Nadu since 2023-24. The State Government of Tamil Nadu 
has not submitted any proposal for gap funding from National CAMPA under MISHTI.

84. SHRI PRABHAKAR REDDY VEMIREDDY: 
SHRI MAGUNTA SREENIVASULU REDDY: 
 
 
Will the Minister of CULTURE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of the list of monuments recognised as Monuments of National 
Importance across the country, State-wise especially from Andhra Pradesh; 
(b) whether the Government has considered rationalising the existing list, if so, the 
details of the list of monuments proposed to be added, deleted and presently 
removed State-wise especially from Andhra Pradesh; 
(c) the details of the extent of funds allocated, released and utilised for the 
maintenance and restoration of monuments of national importance during the 
last five years, State-wise, especially in Andhra Pradesh; 
(d) whether the Government has undertaken any steps to allow private entities to 
sponsor the maintenance/restoration of monuments of national importance, if so, 
the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; and 
(e) whether the Government has undertaken any steps to increase visitor footfall at 
monuments of national importance, if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons 
therefor? 
 
                                                             ANSWER 
   THE MINISTER OF CULTURE AND TOURISM 
       (SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) 3685 ancient monuments and archaeological sites and remains of national 
importance are looked after by Archeological Survey of India (ASI), out of which 
135 are located in the state of Andhra Pradesh. Details are given at Annexure-I. 
(b) The declaration of ancient monuments or archaeological sites and remains as of 
National importance is a regular process undertaken according to provisions of 
the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958. 
Details of the monuments as well as archaeological sites and remains added 
and removed during the last three years from list of monuments and sites are 
given at Annexure-II. 
(c) Details of allocation and expenditure incurred for conservation, preservation and 
environmental development of protected monuments and sites in the country including 
Andhra Pradesh during the last five years are given at Annexure-III. 
(d) The Adopt-A-Heritage 2.0 programme, exclusively for protected monuments was 
launched in September 2023 to create a framework for engagement with private/public 
sector companies and NGOs/ Trusts/ Societies, etc., to develop/provide amenities at 
protected monuments to enhance visitors' experience and make them visitor-friendly. 

Details of monuments and private/public sector companies under the scheme are given 
are at Annexure-IV. 
 
(e) ASI organizes cultural awareness programmes on various occasions like World 
Heritage Day, World Heritage Week, International Museums Day, Republic Day, 
Independence Day, Gandhi Jayanti, etc. through exhibitions, workshops and other 
programmes involving school & college students and general public, etc.  
 
Tourist facilities are provided as per the requirement and feasibility at various protected 
monuments and sites including World Heritage properties in the country. Further, 
amenities like drinking water, toilets and facilities like benches, pathways, wheel chairs, 
ramps, signages, Braille signages, etc. are provided to extend better visitor experience 
and make them visitor friendly.  Providing such facilities and upgrading them is a 
continuous phenomenon.

MINISTRY OF CULTURE

TO BE ANSWERED ON 01.12.2025 
 
PRESERVATION OF CULTURAL HERITAGE OF UTTARAKHAND 
 
 
†85. SHRI TRIVENDRA SINGH RAWAT: 
   Will the Minister of CULTURE be pleased to state: 
 
  (a) whether the Government has formulated any scheme for preservation of the cultural 
heritage of the Uttarakhand State; 
(b) the efforts being made to promote cultural festivals and folk art; 
(c) whether any financial assistance is being provided to the local artists; and 
(d) the extent to which these initiatives have helped in conservation of cultural heritage? 
ANSWER 
 MINISTER OF CULTURE AND TOURISM 
     (SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT)                                           
(a) 
& 
(b) 
There are 43 centrally protected monuments/sites under the care and maintenance of 
Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) in the state of Uttarakhand. Conservation of these 
monuments/sites is taken up as per the need and availability of resources subject to the 
National Policy for Conservation, and these monuments/sites are in a good state of 
preservation.  
The Sangeet Natak Akademi is committed to the preservation and promotion of folk, 
traditional and tribal performing arts through its schemes. The Akademi has organized 
the following festivals in Uttarakhand in the recent past: 
 Kala Dharohar - a series of Workshops dedicated to Meera Bai at Suyalbari, 
Nainital, 23-24 August 2024 
 Kala Dharohar - a series of Workshops dedicated to Meera Bai at Dehradun 14-
15 November 2024 
 Kala Dharohar - a series of Workshops dedicated to Meera Bai at Tapowan, Tehri 
Garhwal, 14-15 November 2024 
 Kala Dharohar, a series of Workshops dedicated to Meera Bai at Chamoli, 11-12 
December 2024 
 Kala Pravah- The Akademi organized two-day festivals of music and dance on 06 
July 2024 at the Kasar Devi Temple at Almora 
 Kala Pravaah, Mandir Utsav Series, in June 2023 at Kasar Devi Mandir at  
Almora.         
 
Cont….2.. 

 
-2- 
 
To protect, promote and preserve various forms of folk art and culture throughout the 
country, the Government of India has also set up seven Zonal Cultural Centres (ZCCs) 
These ZCCs organize various cultural activities and programmes on regular basis in their 
member States. As Uttarakhand is a member State of both North Zone Cultural Centre 
(NCZC), Patiala and North Central Zone Cultural Centre (NCZCC), Prayagraj, cultural 
festivals and art promotion in Uttarakhand are organized by these ZCCs. 
 
Besides, Ministry of Culture also organizes Rashtriya Sanskriti Mahotsavs (RSMs) at 
national level through these ZCCs where a large number of folk & tribal artists including 
local artists from all over India are engaged to showcase their talents to spread awareness 
about our rich cultural heritage. 
 
Further, Sangeet Natak Akademi has started the following four training programmes of 
performing art forms of Uttarakhand under the scheme “Kala Deeksha” (Guru Shishya 
Parampara) 
- Folk Songs of Garhwal region (Padavani & Manglik Geet) under Guru Ganga 
Devi Rana, Chamoli. 
- Mashak Been under Guru Harish Lal, Chamoli 
- Hudka under Guru Loveraj Ram, Munsiyari. 
- Folk Songs of Kumaon region (Neoli, Chhapeli, Bhagnaul and Sanskar Geet) 
Pushpa Fartyal, Almora.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS 
 
   LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 87 
ANSWERED ON MONDAY , 01st December, 2025 
AGRAHAYANA 10, 1947 (SAKA) 
 
Shell Companies 
87. Shri K C Venugopal: 
 
Will the Minister of Corporate Affairs be pleased to state: 
(a) The number of shell companies identified and struck off by the 
Government from official records during the last five years; 
(b) Whether any such companies were found involved in money 
laundering or tax evasion, if so, the details thereof; 
(c) The measures taken by the Government to prevent the re -
emergence of such entities under new names; and  
(d) Whether the Government proposes to strengthen inter -agency 
coordination with Enforcement Directorate (ED) and Income Tax 
Department for monitoring such activities and if so, the details 
thereof? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS AND 
MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS. 
               (SHRI HARSH MALHOTRA) 
(a) to (c) : The term ‘Shell Company’ is not defined in the Companies 
Act, 2013 (Act). However, from time to time, this Ministry carries 
out Strike -Off drive under section 248(1) for striking off such 
companies which are not carrying on any business or operation for 
a period of two immediately preceding financial years and has not 
made any application within such period for obtaining the status of 
a dormant company under section 455 of the Act or the subscribers 
to the memorandum have not paid the subscription wh ich they 
hadundertaken to pay at the time of incorporation of a company 
and a declaration to this effect that not been filed within one 
hundred and eighty days of its incorporation under sub -section (1) 

of section 10A of the Act. The last strike -off drive was carried out 
in the year 2022-23. 
 
Further, under section 248(2) of the Companies Act, 2013 such 
companies which voluntarily seek removal of their name from the 
Registrar of Companies after extinguishing all its liabilities are 
struck-off by following due process in the prescribed manner.  
 
The Companies Act, 2013 and rules made thereunder contain 
adequate provisions for ensuring accountability and transparency 
in the management of companies. It provides for accountability for 
management of companies through key managerial personnel, 
Board of directors and shareholders. The Act & Rules require 
companies to maintain books of account, various returns and

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CULTURE 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO-89 
 
ANSWERED ON 01.12.2025 
 
PRESERVATION OF CULTURAL HERITAGE AND FOLK ART OF BHARATPUR 
 
†89. SMT. SANJNA JATAV: 
 
Will the Minister of CULTURE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware of the status and continued neglect of preservation and 
promotion of the traditional cultural heritage and folk art of Bharatpur district of 
Rajasthan, which is gradually diminishing; 
(b) if so, the details of the schemes aimed at preserving cultural heritage, providing financial 
assistance to local artists and promoting cultural tourism; and 
(c) if not, the reasons for the inadequate Governmental attention and lack of effective 
cultural development in the district? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF CULTURE AND TOURISM  
(SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) To protect, promote and preserve various forms of folk art & culture and to preserve 
and promote the traditional cultural heritage of the country including Rajasthan, the 
Government of India has set up seven Zonal Cultural Centres (ZCCs). Rajasthan is a member 
State of West Zone Cultural Centre (WZCC), Udaipur; North Zone Cultural Centre (NZCC), 
Patiala and North Central Zone Cultural Centre (NCZCC), Prayagraj. These ZCCs organize 
various cultural activities and programmes on regular basis in their member States including 
the State of Rajasthan. The ZCCs also implement number of schemes viz. Award to Young 
Talented Artistes, Guru Shishya Parampara, Theatre Rejuvenation, Research & 
Documentation, Shilpgram, Octave, and National Cultural Exchange Programme to promote 
the cultural heritage of their member States including the State of Rajasthan. 
 
 Recently, WZCC, NZCC & NCZCC have also undertaken the revival of vanishing art 
forms viz. Bhapang Wadan, Bahurupi Kala, Sarangi Vadan, Tamasha Folk Theatre, Sanskrut 
Naatya, Kadtal Vadan, Kalbelia Dance, Dhrupad Gayan, Mand Gayan, Madheran Art, 
Rawan Hatha Instrument, Mewati Lok Gayan and Kuchamani Khayal Lok Natya of 
Rajasthan including Bharatpur.  
 
 Ministry of Culture has also organized Vilupt Lok Evam Janjatiya Kala Utthan 
Mahotsav (festival of vanishing art forms) by all the ZCCs at Divisional level across all 7 
Zones in collaboration with Ministry of Textiles, Cultural Departments of State Govts, 
Folklore and Cultural Studies Departments of various State/ Central Universities.   
 
 WZCC, NZCC & NCZCC engage folk artists from their member States including 
Rajasthan during various cultural activities & programmes organized by them for which they 
are paid honorarium, TA/DA, boarding & lodging, local transport etc.  
         
 
 

(b) Ministry of Culture runs Guru-Shishya Parampara (Repertory Grant) Scheme under 
which financial support is provided to folk artists of all genres of performing arts viz. musical 
groups, dance groups, theatre groups including children theatre, music ensembles etc. Under 
the scheme, the amount of assistance for Guru (leader of the Group) is Rs. 15,000/- per 
month and for the Shishya is Rs. 2,000-10,000/- per month depending upon the age of the 
artist. 
 
 To promote the traditional fair festivals of the country including Rajasthan, Ministry 
of Culture runs a scheme viz. Cultural Function and Production Grant Scheme (CFPG) under 
which financial assistance is provided to organizations for organizing Seminars, Conferences, 
Research, Workshops, Festivals, Exhibitions, Symposia, Production of Dance, Drama-
Theatre, Music etc. The grant released to the organizations located in Rajasthan under this 
scheme during the last three years is as under: 
 
Sl. No. Year No. of organizations   Amount 
i. 2022-23 48 Rs. 81.16 lakh 
ii. 2023-24 58 Rs. 82.28 lakh 
iii. 2024-25 40 Rs. 61.55 lakh 
 
 Ministry of Culture through its ZCCs organizes Rashtriya Sanskriti Mahotsavs 
(RSMs) at national level in the country by providing a platform to a large number of folk 
artists from all over India including the State of Rajasthan who showcase their talents during 
the event. Till date, 14 RSMs and 04 Zonal Level RSMs have been organized by the Ministry 
of Culture. The 14th RSM was held at Bikaner, Rajasthan from 25th February to 5th March, 
2023. The event was inaugurated by H.E. the President of India.  
 
 The first Zonal Level Rashtriya Sanskriti Mahotsav was organized at Kota, Rajasthan 
on 5th September, 2023. The then Hon’ble Vice President of India graced the event.   
(c) Does not arise.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO-9 
ANSWERED ON 01/12/2025 
 
Absentee Vice-Chancellor of Tezpur University 
9. Shri Pradyut Bordoloi: 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has taken any steps to address the absence of Vice-Chancellor since 22nd 
September 2025, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether the Government has received the report of the Fact -Finding Committee constituted by 
Governor of Assam-cum-Chancellor of Tezpur University to examine the serious allegations regarding 
the functioning of the Vice-Chancellor, if so, the details and the findings thereof; 
(c) whether any Central team has been deputed to assess the prevailing administrative situation in 
Tezpur University, if so, the details and the findings of their visit thereof; 
(d) whether it is a fact that large-scale irregularities have been reported in the appointment of security 
guards, violation of labour laws and procurement of library books and e-resources, including inflated 
quotations, irregular tendering and possible vendor collusion, if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) whether any steps have been taken by the Government to resolve the administrative deadlock 
caused by the prolonged absence, if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
(a) to (e): Central Universities are autonomous institutions established under Acts of Parliament and 
governed in accordance with the provisions of their respective Acts, Statutes, and Ordinances. As per 
the Tezpur University Act, 1993, if the office of the Vice -Chancellor becomes vacant, the Pro -Vice-
Chancellor shall perform the duties of the Vice -Chancellor. It further provi des that if the Pro -Vice-
Chancellor is not available, the senior-most Professor shall perform the duties of the Vice-Chancellor 
until a new Vice-Chancellor assumes office or until the existing Vice-Chancellor attends to the duties 
of his office, as the case may be.  
The Fact-Finding Committee constituted by the Hon’ble Governor of Assam has submitted its report 
to the Hon’ble Governor (ex officio Chancellor of Tezpur University).

 Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the details of the number of projects sanctioned under the Assistance to 
Central Agencies (ACA) for Tourism Infrastructure Development Scheme 
during the last five years, year, Central agenc y, State, and district -
wise, particularly for Andhra Pradesh including Kakinada; 
(b)  the details of funds allocated, released, and utilised under the said 
Scheme for these projects during the said period, year, Central agency, 
State and district-wise for Andhra Pradesh including Kakinada; 
(c)  whether any new proposals from Central agencies in Andhra Pradesh 
have been received under the Scheme; 
(d)  if so, the details thereof, along with their current status as approved or 
pending and details of the funds allocated for approved projects; 
(e) whether the Government has undertaken any study or assessment for the 
development of new tourism destinations in coastal areas of the country; 
and 
(f) if so, the details thereof; and if not, the reasons therefor?

Agencies (ACA) for Tourism Infrastructure Development provides  Central 
Financial Assistance to Central Agencies for development of tourism related 
infrastructure. Under the scheme, the Ministry has sanctioned a total of 66 
projects amounting ₹948.78 crore including Andhra Pradesh. Out of these 14 

projects have been sanctioned during the last five years the details of which 
is annexed. 
 
(c) to (d): No new proposals have been received from central agencies in 
Andhra Pradesh under the scheme.   Receiving proposals from the Central 
Agencies for financial assistance for tourism projects is a continuous 
process. The proposals received are examined with ref erence to the 
prescribed guidelines and financial assistance is extended for such projects 
subject to fulfilment of the stipulated conditions and availability of funds. 
 
(e) to (f): The Ministry of Tourism has not undertaken any  study or 
assessment for the development of new tourism destinations in coastal areas 
of the country. However,  the Ministry encourages state

under PRASAD and if so, the details thereof; and 
(j) whether the Government has any specific plan or an in-principle approved 
project for the development of tourism and allied infrastructure (like 
Tourist Facilitation Centers, last -mile connectivity and promotion 
activities) in Mohanlalganj Lok Sabha Constit uency for the next two 
financial years and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF TOURISM               (SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) and (b):  The Ministry of Tourism through its ongoing schemes of 
‘Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual, Heritage Augmentation Drive 
(PRASHAD)’ and Swadesh Darshan, complements the efforts of the State 
Governments (SGs)/UT Administrations (UTs) by exte nding financial 
assistance to them for developing tourism related infrastructure in the 
country, including the State Government of Andhra Pradesh and Uttar 
Pradesh. 
 
Since the launch of the PRASHAD Scheme launch in January 2015, the 
Ministry has sanctioned 54 projects in 28 States/UTs with an estimated cost 
of ₹1726.74 Crore. 
 
Under the Swadesh Darshan Scheme, the Ministry of Tourism has 
sanctioned a total number of 76 projects under different thematic circuits in 
the country for a total sanctioned cost of ₹5290.30 Crore.  
 
The Swadesh Darshan scheme has been revamped as ‘Swadesh 
Darshan 2.0’ (SD 2.0) with the objective to develop sustainable and 
responsible tourism destinations. Till date, 53 projects have been sanctioned 
by the Ministry under SD 2.0 at a total sanctioned cost of ₹2,208.27 Crore. 
 
The details of the projects under PRASHAD, Swadesh Darshan Scheme 
and Swadesh Darshan 2.0, are given in the Annexure-I. 
 
(c) and (d):  Under the PRASHAD Scheme, infrastructure development is 
undertaken in an inclusive, integrated and sustainable manner that focuses 
on livelihoods, skills, cleanliness, security, accessibility, and service delivery. 
The scheme contributes to employment gen eration while also enhancing 

awareness and fostering skill and capacity development of the local 
communities. 
 
(e): The Ministry of Tourism has put in place the Scheme of “Capacity Building 
for Service Providers” (CBSP) which provides education, training and 
certification to the tourism service providers and hospitality sector including 
women & youth, to upgrade manpower at every strata of the tourism industry 
in order to capitalise the vast tourism potential of the country to the fullest 
and provide professional expertise to the local populace as well as create 
fresh opportunities in the tourism sector both in urban as well as rural areas. 
 
(f): Under the PRASHAD Scheme, the Ministry of Tourism has developed 
tourism infrastructure for improving tourist amenities and tourist experience 
at pilgrimage sites. 
 
Some of the components/ interventions approved under the PRASHAD 
Scheme aimed at improving/ integrating tourism, transport and sanitation  
facilities includes upgradation of tourist arrival areas with Tourist Facilitation 
Centres, parking; provision of bas ic amenities like waiting halls and 
cloakrooms and development of utility infrastructure such as solid waste 
management,  bio -toilets, drinking water facilities, improved drainage 
networks, dustbins and pious waste management facilities, landscaping and 
beautification, etc. 
 
In addition, to improve connectivity and accessibility to the site, several 
components have been sanctioned including approach road development, 
road widening and beautification, development of destination entry points, 
ramps, railings, dedicated wheelchai r-accessible facilities, provisions for e -
vehicles and lifts, etc. 
 
(g): Under the Swadesh Darshan Scheme, out of 76 sanctioned projects, 75 
projects have been physically completed and under the PRASHAD Scheme, 
out of 54 sanctioned projects, 32 projects have been physically completed. 
The details are provided in the Annexure-II. 
 
(h):  As per the Report on Evaluation of Central Sector Scheme PRASHAD by 
IIM Rohtak in the year 2021, the Scheme has helped in increasing the visitor 
satisfaction, ease of travel and aesthetical aspects of the selected heritage 
sites. Also, the report mentioned  that the Scheme has led to increase in the 
positive overall visitor user experience. 

 
(i) and (j): Receiving proposals from the State Governments/UT 
Administrations for financial assistance for tourism projects is a continuous 
process. The proposals received are examined with reference to the 
prescribed guidelines and financial assistance i s extended for such projects 
subject to fulfilment of the stipulated conditions and availability of funds. 
 
No proposal is under consideration of the Ministry of Tourism under the 
PRASHAD Scheme for development of tourism infrastructure in Mohanlalganj 
Lok Sabha Constituency of Uttar Pradesh. However, the Ministry of Tourism 
has sanctioned various projects in Uttar Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh, the list 
of which is given in the Annexure-III.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 94 
  ANSWERED ON 01.12.2025 
 
CRAFTSMEN TRAINING SCHEME IN UTTAR PRADESH 
 
94. Dr. Bhola Singh:  
Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP be pleased to state:  
(a)  the number of Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) and National Skill Training Institutes (NSTIs) 
currently imparting training under the Craftsmen Training Scheme in Uttar Pradesh; 
(b) the number of ITIs, total trades offered and trainees enrolled in Bulandshahr district during the current 
year;  
(c) whether the Government proposes to upgrade infrastructure, introduce new -age trades and 
modernise training labs in Bulandshahr; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof along with the timeline for implementation? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT 
AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
(a) The Directorate General of Training (DGT), under the  Ministry of Skill Development and 
Entrepreneurship (MSDE) implements the Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) through a network of 
Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) and National Skill Training Institutes (NSTIs)  for skilling the youth of 
the country. In the State of Uttar Pradesh, a total of 3,300 ITIs (Government - 294 and Private - 3,006) 
and 03 NSTIs are currently imparting training under CTS. 
 
(b) In the Bulandshahr district of Uttar Pradesh, at present, 41 ITIs (Government - 08 and Private- 33) are 
running and offering training in 33 CTS courses.  A total of 4,834 trainees have been enrolled in the ITIs 
in the Bulandshahr district during the current session (2025–26). 
 
(c)  and (d) The Cabinet has approved PM SETU (Prime Minister’s Scheme for Empowerment through 
Technology Upgradation), at an estimated cost  of ₹60,000 crore (Central Share: ₹30,000 crore, State 
Share: ₹20,000 crore, and Industry Share: ₹10,000 crore). The scheme aims to upgrade 1,000 ITIs 
through hub -and-spoke arrangements, focusing on outcome orientation in collaboration with state 
governments and industry. 
 
Under the scheme, course content and design is proposed to be aligned with industry skill needs, and 
new courses are proposed to be introduced to address emerging areas, with the objective of creating a 
future-ready skilled workforce to meet the dynamic ne eds of India’s economy and enhance industrial 
value addition. The scheme focuses on pan-India level implementation based on proposals received from 
States/UTs, including the State of Uttar Pradesh. The Cabinet has approved implementation of scheme 
till Financial Year 2029-30.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 95 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 01.12.2025 
 
STATUS OF E-SHRAM CARD 
 
95.  SHRI MALAIYARASAN D:  
 
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state:  
 
(a)the details of the total number of e-Shram cards issued across the 
country, State/UT-wise particularly the number of registrations in 
Kallakurichi Lok Sabha constituency in Tamil Nadu;  
(b)whether the Government has a mechanism to verify and update the 
occupational and income details of workers registered on the e -
Shram portal, and if so, the details thereof; 
(c)the details of the registered unorganised workers under e -Shram 
who have benef ited from welfare schemes, insurance or direct 
financial support since the launch of the scheme;  
(d)whether there is any plan to integrate e -Shram data with State 
Welfare Schemes and if so, whether the Government has 
considered any proposals from State Go vernment of Tamil Nadu; 
and  
(e)the details of the steps taken by the Government to ensure that 
migrant workers, women workers and those in informal sectors are 
fully covered under the scheme in the country particularly in rural 
and urban areas of Tamil Nadu especially in Kallakurichi Lok Sabha 
Constituency? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a) to (e): The Ministry of Labour and Employment launched eShram 
portal (eshram.gov.in) on 26th August 2021 for creation of a 
comprehensive National Database of Unorganised Workers (NDUW) 
seeded with Aadhaar. eShram portal is meant to register and support 
the unorganised workers by providing them a Universal Account 
Number (UAN) on a self -declaration basis.  Further Unorganised 
worker registered on eShram portal can also verify and update their 
occupational and income details on the eShram portal or through 
Common Service Centre (CSC).  
Contd..2/- 

:: 2 :: 
 
  As on 19 th November 2025, over 31.36 crore unorganised 
workers have already registered on eShram portal and over 94.69 
lakhs eShram cards have been issued in the State of Tamil Nadu 
including 2,45,592 registrations of unorganised workers in 
Kallakurichi constituency in Tamil Nadu. 
 
  State-wise details of number of unorganised workers 
registered at the eShram portal across the country is at annexure-I. 
 
  The details of the registered unorganised workers under 
eShram who have benefited from various welfare schemes is at 
annexure-II. 
 
  To facilitate data driven implementation, data sharing 
guidelines have been formulated and issued for sharing eShram data 
to the Labour Departments of States and Union Territories. In 
accordance with these guidelines, eShram data has been made 
available with States/ UTs Labour Departments and BOCW Welfare 
Boards to support targeted delivery and saturation of welfare 
schemes for unorganised workers.  
 
  To enhance registrations under the eShram initiative and 
ensure wider coverage of unorganised workers across the country 
including migrant workers and women workers, the Government has 
adopted a comprehensive strategy. In addition to enabling self -
registration through the web portal and mob ile application, assisted 
registration modes have been introduced via Common Service 
Centres (CSCs), State Seva Kendras (SSKs), and the UMANG platform 
to facilitate easy access for workers. The Ministry of Labour and 
Employment is conducting targeted aware ness campaigns 
comprising registration drives, community outreach programs and 
locally tailored communication efforts. To strengthen outreach, the 
Ministry leverages social media channels to disseminate videos, 
tutorials, and other informative content, mak ing the initiative more 
accessible and engaging. 
 
  To further enhance the availability and accessibility of 
eShram and its associated services to unorganised workers, the 
Ministry of Labour and Employment officially launched the eShram 
mobile application on 24th February 2025. This application facilitates 
real-time access to welfare schemes integrated with the eShram 
platform, thereby significantly strengthening both accessibility and 
user convenience.

(SAKA) 
 
“Mutual Funds” 
QUESTION 
 
96. SHRI NAVEEN JINDAL 
 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether it is a fact that there is more than 100% increase in the investments in mutual 
funds and about 70% increase in the pension and equity in the country during the last 
decade, if so, the reasons therefor; 
 
(b) whether there has been a decrease in fixed deposits, savings and current accounts deposits, 
if so, the details and the reasons therefor; and  
 
(c) the likely impact of these trends in short, medium and long terms, respectively, on the 
economy? 
 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR FINANCE 
(SH. PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
*** 
(a) & (c): The Assets Under Management (AUM) of Mutual Funds, National Pension 
System (NPS) and overall market capitalization of listed companies increased by 508%, 
1685%, and 314% respectively during the FY 2014–15 to 2024–25. The growth is 
mainly driven by  strong macroeconomic condition, improved corporate earnings,  
effective regulatory reforms,  increased retail participation and improved accessibility 
through digital public infrastructure . These developments are expected to strengthen

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION AND LITERACY 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO – 97 
 
ANSWERED ON 01/12/2025 
 
Food Poisoning Incident in School Hostels in Andhra Pradesh 
 
97. Shri Maddila Gurumoorthy: 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has taken cognizance of repeated food poisoning 
incidents in Andhra Pradesh Government schools/hostels reportedly caused  by 
unclean RO plants, stagnant water tanks and unhygienic kitchen conditions, if so, the 
details thereof; 
(b) whether any preventive audits, inspections, or corrective measures have been 
initiated by the Government or in coordination with State Education Departments to 
ensure food and water safety in such institutions, and if so, the details thereof; 
(c) if not, the reasons for the inaction; and 
(d) whether the Government proposes to introduce a mandatory quarterly inspection 
and digital reporting system f or all government and welfare hostels to ensure 
compliance with food safety and hygiene standards and if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
(a) to (d): Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman (PM POSHAN) Scheme is 
implemented in partnership with States/ UTs for providing one hot cooked and 
nutritious meal to children studying in Balvatika (just before class I) and the classes I 
to VIII of Government and Government-aided schools on all school working days. The 
overall responsibility for smooth functioning of the scheme including providing hot 

cooked and nutritious meal to the eligible children and day -to-day administration lies 
with the State Governments and Union Territory Administrations.  
 
Government of India has issued detailed guidelines on quality, safety and 
hygiene to ensure serving of good quality nutritious meal under the Scheme.  All the 
States/ UTs are advised to adhere to these Guidelines. These guidelines are available 
on official website  https://pmposhan.education.gov.in. These guidelines, inter alia , 
provide instructions to schools to procure Agmark quality and branded items for 
preparation of meals, training to Cook -cum-Helpers, tasting of meals by members of 
School Management Committee including at least one teacher before serving the hot 
meal to children. Further, it provides for testing of food samples by Government Food 
Research Laboratory or any laboratory accredited or recognized by law to ensure that 
the meals meet nutritional standards and quality. The Food Corporation of India (FCI) 
is given responsibility for making available food grains of best available quality, 
meeting the parameters of Fair Average Quality (FAQ). The Guidelines provide, inter-
alia, for training of Cook -cum-Helpers on nutrition, cooking processes, health and 
hygiene, preparation of raw grains and vegetables, recipes, serving skills etc. States/ 
UTs provide t raining to CCHs in collaboration with Institutes of Hotel Management, 
Food Craft Institutes, FSSAI, State Universities etc. Many States/ UTs conduct the 
Cooking Competitions and also give cash prizes to the winners to encourage them to 
cook varied and nutritious meals. The States and UTs are encouraged to decide menu 
suitable to the local conditions within the prescribed nutrition and food norms and to 
procure locally grown food items like millets, vegetables, condiments etc. The 
guidelines also envisage for all children in the school to wash their hands with soap.  
 
As per information received from the State Government of Andhra Pradesh, a 
few incidents of water/food contamination have occurred, and affected students were 
admitted to the hospitals immediately, and after treatment, all of them were discharged 
safely. As a follow up, special inspections have been conducted in all Government 
Hostels in the State and action has been taken to rectify the defects. 
 
Further, FSSAI has prepared Food Safety Guidebook for Teachers/Students. 
The booklet provides with the detailed information of how to conduct the different test 
on food adulteration. FSSAI through its social media channel has created a dedicated 

playlist “How to check for adulteration”. FSSAI al so have mobile food testing vans 
called Food Safety on Wheels (FSW) to reach remote areas and conduct training and 
awareness activities as well. 
 
POSHAN Maah/ POSHAN Pakhwada is celebrated by States and UTs 
facilitating community mobilisation and ensuring schools undertake meaningful 
activities such as special School Management Committee (SMC) meetings, awareness 
campaigns on nutrition and hygiene. Various other activities such as quiz, painting 
competition, rally, nukkad natak for disseminating the informa tion on use of millets, 
handwash, balance diet and importance of green leafy vegetables etc. are also 
organized at school level. 
The State Government of Andhra Pradesh has issued Standard Operating 
Procedure (SoP) for maintenance of hostels, child safety and security, food safety, 
water safety, personal health and hygiene, reporting of untoward incidents and crisis 
management. Guidelines have also been issued for cleaning water tanks, maintenance 
of RO Plants, safety, security, health, mental well -being, a nd protection of all girl 
students residing in Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalayas (KGBVs).

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 99 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 01.12.2025 
 
Presence of Microplastics in Rivers, Lakes and Coastal Waters 
 
99:   DR. M P ABDUSSAMAD SAMADANI: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a)  whether studies have been conducted on the presence of microplastics in Indian rivers, 
lakes and coastal waters; 
(b) the extent of microplastic  accumulation in aquatic organisms and its ecological and 
health impact; 
(c)  the steps taken by the Government to regulate sources such as single -use plastics, 
synthetic textiles and cosmetic microbeads; and 
(d)  whether the Government has any plan to establish a national framework for monitoring 
and mitigating microplastic pollution in coordination with State Pollution Control 
Boards and scientific institutions? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI V ARDHAN SINGH) 
 
 (a) to ( d):  Studies undertaken by national institutions have shown the presence of 
microplastics in riverine and coastal zones. In order to reduce pollution caused by littered and 
unmanaged plastic waste, which includes microplastics, the Ministry of Environment, Forest 
and Climate Change has already prohibited identified single use plastic items, which have low 
utility and high li ttering potential, with effect from 1 July, 2022.  As per details provided by 
SPCB/PCC and details available at SUP compliance monitoring portal, a total of 8,61,740 
inspections have been conducted and 1985 tonnes of banned single use plastic items have been 
seized and a total of Rs. 19.82 crores of fine has been levied, since July, 2022.  
 
Further, the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change has also notified the 
Guidelines on Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) for plastic packaging vide Pla stic 
Waste Management (Amendment) Rules, 2022, on 16th February, 2022. The Guidelines 
stipulate mandatory targets on EPR, recycling of plastic packaging waste, reuse of rigid plastic 
packaging and use of recycled plastic content. The guidelines provide for  moving towards 
sustainable plastic packaging and reducing the plastic foot print. 165 lakh tonnes of plastic 

packaging waste has been recycled, after the EPR Guidelines on plastic packaging have come 
into force in 2022.  
 
Also, Swachh Bharat Mission provi des central assistance for solid waste management 
including plastic waste management in urban and rural areas of the country. The Government 
of India supplement s the efforts of the States/UTs by providing financial and technical 
assistance in addressing th e challenges of river pollution through schemes/programmes such 
as National River Conservation Plan and Namami Gange programme. Different pollution 
abatement works inter alia, include interception and diversion of raw sewage, sewerage system, 
and establishment of sewage treatment plants, as per scheme guidelines.  
 
Further, vide Amendment No. 2, of Indian Standard lS 4707 (Part 2): 2017, Classification of 
Cosmetic Raw Materials and Adjuncts ( Fourth Revision) notified in November 2017, under 
Annex A at Sr. No. 1373 it has stated that Plastic microbeads: 5 mm or less, water insoluble, 
solid plastic particles used to exfoliate or cleanse in rinse -off personal care products are not 
recognized as safe for use in Cosmetics. The raw materials specified in Annex A of the Indian 
Standard IS: 4707 Part 2, as amended from time to time, shall not be added in cosmetic product, 
as per the Cosmetics Rules issued under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940.   
 
The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, celebrated World Environment Day 
2025 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, on 5 th June 2025, with the slogan ‘One Nation, One 
Mission: End Plastic Pollution’. As part of one month long pre-campaign activities undertaken 
before World Environment Day 2025, around 69,000 events were organized in which around 
21 lakh people participated across the country. The National Plastic Pollution Reduction 
Campaign (NPPRC) was also launched for the period 5th June to 31st October 2025. The  
Campaign included activities to reduce plastic pollution in urban and rural areas under 
Swachhta Hi Sewa programme. The activities also included focus on reducing use of avoidable 
single use plastics in government offices especially during Special Campaign 5.0.
